      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: Notably, EWS-FLI1 fusion genes acted in a positive feedback loop to maintain the expression of PARP1, which was required for EWS-FLI-mediated transcription, thereby enforcing oncogene-dependent sensitivity to PARP-1 inhibition.
      explanation: >-
        Ewing cellular studies support reciprocal dependence of fusion transcription and PARP1.
- name: Tumor-Stroma IL-6/STAT3 Signaling
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    In flow-perfusion coculture, mesenchymal stromal cells and Ewing tumor cells respond to biophysical
    cues through IL-6/STAT3 signaling and altered drug response. This established-tumor microenvironment
    mechanism is distinct from IGF-1/YAP1 developmental initiation.
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: interleukin-6-mediated signaling pathway
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0070102
      label: interleukin-6-mediated signaling pathway
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: mesenchymal stem cell
    term:
      id: CL:0000134
      label: mesenchymal stem cell
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:27923328
    reference_title: Modeling Stroma-Induced Drug Resistance in a Tissue-Engineered Tumor Model of Ewing Sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Here, we demonstrate that these same biophysical cues-modeled by coculturing ES cells and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in 3D scaffolds within a flow perfusion bioreactor-activate interleukin-6 and transcription factor Stat3.
    explanation: >-
      A tissue-engineered tumor-stroma coculture demonstrates IL-6/STAT3 activation under biophysical
      stimulation.
  downstream:
  - target: Tumor Cell Proliferation and Survival
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    hypothesis_groups:
    - canonical_fusion_enhanceropathy_model
    description: >-
      Stromal cytokine signaling modifies tumor-cell survival and drug response in a tissue-engineered
      model.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:27923328
      reference_title: Modeling Stroma-Induced Drug Resistance in a Tissue-Engineered Tumor Model of Ewing Sarcoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: Here, we demonstrate that these same biophysical cues-modeled by coculturing ES cells and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) in 3D scaffolds within a flow perfusion bioreactor-activate interleukin-6 and transcription factor Stat3.
      explanation: >-
        A tissue-engineered tumor-stroma coculture demonstrates IL-6/STAT3 activation under biophysical
        stimulation.
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - IL-6/STAT3 activation
- name: Hybrid Mesenchymal Tumor States and Matrix Deposition
  description: >-
    Ewing tumors contain coexisting gene-regulatory programs. CD73-positive malignant subpopulations
    can retain fusion-activated genes while expressing normally repressed mesenchymal and extracellular-matrix
    genes. These CAF-like tumor cells deposit matrix near tumor borders and invasive foci. Their
    presence is not proof of a separate fibroblast lineage, and a universal binary fusion-high/fusion-low
    switch does not capture the observed heterogeneity.
  biological_processes:
  - preferred_term: extracellular matrix organization
    modifier: INCREASED
    term:
      id: GO:0030198
      label: extracellular matrix organization
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40667384
    reference_title: Multimodal single-cell analyses reveal distinct fusion-regulated transcriptional programs in Ewing sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: When we examined primary EwS patient tumors, we observed these same regulatory modules were variably enriched both across and within tumors, highlighting the existence of intratumoral heterogeneity in gene regulatory networks.
    explanation: >-
      Single-cell RNA/ATAC analyses identify multiple coexisting regulatory programs rather than
      a single binary fusion-high/fusion-low axis.
  - reference: PMID:37471463
    reference_title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Like Tumor Cells Remodel the Ewing Sarcoma Tumor Microenvironment.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: These cells retained expression of the fusion-activated gene signature alongside high expression of genes that are normally repressed by EWS::FLI1.
    explanation: >-
      CD73-positive CAF-like tumor cells can occupy hybrid transcriptional states; they are malignant
      cells, not automatically nonmalignant fibroblasts.
  - reference: PMID:37471463
    reference_title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Like Tumor Cells Remodel the Ewing Sarcoma Tumor Microenvironment.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Thus, these EwS cells gained mesenchymal properties, including the capacity to deposit ECM, without losing proliferative or tumorigenic potential.
    explanation: The source directly links the hybrid malignant-cell state to extracellular-matrix deposition. The annotation does not relabel these malignant cells as ordinary fibroblasts.
- name: Osseous Tumor Expansion and Bone Destruction
  description: >-
    In osseous Ewing sarcoma, infiltrative tumor growth destroys the affected bone and can extend
    through cortex into soft tissue. Local structural injury contributes to pain, swelling and fracture
    risk. These consequences are specific to osseous or bone-involving disease; treatment can also
    contribute to later fractures.
  locations:
  - preferred_term: bone tissue
    term:
      id: UBERON:0002481
      label: bone tissue
  notes: >-
    Bone tissue is already explicitly bound to UBERON:0002481. The cited radiographic
    destruction does not isolate osteoclast-mediated resorption, so no osteoclast cell-type
    or bone-resorption process annotation is inferred from this imaging observation.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25691401
    reference_title: "Diagnosis and treatment of Ewing sarcoma of the bone: a review article."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: In ES of the bone, plain radiographs exhibit permeative and infiltrative destruction of the affected bone
    explanation: >-
      Clinical imaging review supports a destructive osseous growth mechanism, distinct from extraskeletal
      disease.
  downstream:
  - target: Bone Pain
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - local tissue injury and nociceptive stimulation
    description: >-
      Destructive local tumor growth can produce pain; the precise nociceptive pathway is not inferred
      from a specific molecular study.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:25691401
      reference_title: "Diagnosis and treatment of Ewing sarcoma of the bone: a review article."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: OTHER
      snippet: Patients with ES exhibit local symptoms such as tumor mass formation, induration, pain, swelling, venous dilation, and hyperemia.
      explanation: >-
        Clinical review connects local growth with pain and swelling.
  - target: Pathologic Fracture
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - loss of structural bone integrity
    description: >-
      Bone involvement weakens the skeleton and predisposes to fracture. Disease-related and post-treatment
      fractures require separate interpretation.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:11902298
      reference_title: Fractures in pediatric Ewing sarcoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: Fracture occurred in 14 (15%) of 93 patients with long-bone ESFT, most commonly in the femur.
      explanation: >-
        Retrospective long-bone cohort supports the complication, with restricted anatomy and historical
        treatment.
- name: EZH2-Associated Differentiation Repression
  description: >-
    EWS-FLI1 induces EZH2, which contributes to repression of differentiation-associated genes and
    maintenance of an undifferentiated state. Genetic depletion impairs clonogenicity and tumorigenicity
    in preclinical systems. This dependency is distinct from the heterogeneous PRC2 changes following
    STAG2 loss and does not imply that every Ewing tumor will respond to an EZH2 inhibitor.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: EZH2
    term:
      id: hgnc:3527
      label: EZH2
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:19289832
    reference_title: EZH2 is a mediator of EWS/FLI1 driven tumor growth and metastasis blocking endothelial and neuro-ectodermal differentiation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Here, we found EWS/FLI1 bound to the EZH2 promoter in vivo, and induced EZH2 expression in ET and mesenchymal stem cells.
    explanation: >-
      Chromatin binding and expression experiments support fusion-associated EZH2 induction; in vivo
      here describes binding within cells, not an animal efficacy result.
  - reference: PMID:19289832
    reference_title: EZH2 is a mediator of EWS/FLI1 driven tumor growth and metastasis blocking endothelial and neuro-ectodermal differentiation.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Subsequent microarray analysis of EZH2 knock down, HDAC-inhibitor treatment and confirmation in independent assays revealed an undifferentiated phenotype maintained by EZH2 in ET.
    explanation: >-
      Cellular perturbation supports maintenance of an undifferentiated transcriptional state.
  downstream:
  - target: Blocked Differentiation
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_KNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    intermediate_mechanisms:
    - repression of differentiation-associated genes
    hypothesis_groups:
    - canonical_fusion_enhanceropathy_model
    description: >-
      EZH2-associated repression maintains an undifferentiated state in Ewing experimental systems.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:19289832
      reference_title: EZH2 is a mediator of EWS/FLI1 driven tumor growth and metastasis blocking endothelial and neuro-ectodermal differentiation.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: Subsequent microarray analysis of EZH2 knock down, HDAC-inhibitor treatment and confirmation in independent assays revealed an undifferentiated phenotype maintained by EZH2 in ET.
      explanation: >-
        Cellular perturbation supports maintenance of an undifferentiated transcriptional state.
- name: HOXD13-Driven Mesenchymal Plasticity
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  description: >-
    Fusion-created enhancer activity at the HOXD locus induces a developmental transcriptional program.
    HOXD13 activates some genes normally repressed by EWS-FLI1 and shifts cells toward mesenchymal
    and migratory states. This provides a defined modifier of the differentiation block and contributes
    to a continuum of tumor states.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: HOXD13
    term:
      id: hgnc:5136
      label: HOXD13
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:35653119
    reference_title: "EWS::FLI1 and HOXD13 Control Tumor Cell Plasticity in Ewing Sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: We found that EWS::FLI1 creates a de novo GGAA microsatellite enhancer in a developmentally conserved regulatory region of the HOXD locus.
    explanation: >-
      Enhancer perturbation supports fusion-dependent HOXD locus activation.
  - reference: PMID:35653119
    reference_title: "EWS::FLI1 and HOXD13 Control Tumor Cell Plasticity in Ewing Sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: More strikingly, HOXD13 bound and activated EWS::FLI1-repressed genes, leading to adoption of mesenchymal and migratory cell states that are normally suppressed by the fusion.
    explanation: >-
      Supports transcriptional antagonism and a mesenchymal-state modifier rather than uniformly
      blocked differentiation.
  downstream:
  - target: Hybrid Mesenchymal Tumor States and Matrix Deposition
    causal_link_type: INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES
    hypothesis_groups:
    - canonical_fusion_enhanceropathy_model
    description: >-
      HOXD13-mediated antagonism contributes to the mesenchymal transcriptional continuum. It is
      one candidate contributor to hybrid states, not a demonstrated sole cause of CD73 expression
      or matrix deposition.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:35653119
      reference_title: "EWS::FLI1 and HOXD13 Control Tumor Cell Plasticity in Ewing Sarcoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: More strikingly, HOXD13 bound and activated EWS::FLI1-repressed genes, leading to adoption of mesenchymal and migratory cell states that are normally suppressed by the fusion.
      explanation: >-
        Supports transcriptional antagonism and a mesenchymal-state modifier rather than uniformly
        blocked differentiation.
- name: BARD1-Loss and GBP1-Associated DNA-Damage Sensitivity
  mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL
  biological_scale: CELLULAR
  description: >-
    A BARD1-variant patient-derived Ewing cell line and BARD1-depletion experiments show enhanced
    sensitivity to PARP inhibition and radiation. BARD1 loss can increase GBP1 expression, which
    contributes to damage-induced apoptosis in the tested cells. Other signals also induce GBP1,
    so expression is not a specific BARD1-loss marker. This is a bounded experimental modifier of
    treatment response; neither disease-wide BARD1 prevalence, penetrant inherited Ewing
    susceptibility nor a validated clinical predictive biomarker is established.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36187937
    reference_title: BRCA1-associated RING domain-1 (BARD1) loss and GBP1 expression enhance sensitivity to DNA damage in Ewing sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: We demonstrate that PSaRC318 cells, a novel patient-derived cell line harboring a pathogenic BARD1 variant, are sensitive to PARP inhibition and by testing the effect of BARD1 depletion in additional Ewing sarcoma cell lines, we confirm that BARD1 loss enhances cell sensitivity to PARP inhibition plus radiation.
    explanation: >-
      Patient-derived and BARD1-depleted cell models support an experimental modifier, not a
      validated patient biomarker or a ten-percent BARD1 frequency.
  - reference: PMID:36187937
    reference_title: BRCA1-associated RING domain-1 (BARD1) loss and GBP1 expression enhance sensitivity to DNA damage in Ewing sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Here, we demonstrate that GBP1 contributes to the enhanced sensitivity of BARD1 deficient Ewing cells to DNA damage.
    explanation: >-
      GBP1 knockdown reduced radiation- and niraparib-associated apoptosis in PSaRC318 cells; GBP1
      expression is not specific to BARD1 loss.
  genes:
  - preferred_term: BARD1
    term:
      id: hgnc:952
      label: BARD1
  - preferred_term: GBP1
    term:
      id: hgnc:4182
      label: GBP1
mechanistic_hypotheses:
- hypothesis_group_id: canonical_fusion_enhanceropathy_model
  hypothesis_label: Canonical EWS-FLI1 fusion enhanceropathy model
  status: CANONICAL
  description: >-
    The canonical fusion transcriptional program includes BAF-supported GGAA enhancer activation,
    NuRD/LSD1-associated repression, core regulatory circuitry, impaired differentiation and metabolic
    rewiring. CHD4-mediated structural maintenance is a separate survival dependency. Dynamic endogenous
    hubs are a preprint-supported refinement. Fusion dosage and multiple coexisting regulatory modules
    create plasticity; most mechanistic experiments concern EWSR1::FLI1 rather than every FET-ETS
    partner.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25453903
    reference_title: "EWS-FLI1 utilizes divergent chromatin remodeling mechanisms to directly activate or repress enhancer elements in Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Our findings demonstrate how EWS-FLI1 establishes an oncogenic regulatory program governing both tumor survival and differentiation."
    explanation: Supports the canonical fusion enhanceropathy model.
  - reference: PMID:41659683
    reference_title: "Dynamic regulation of endogenous transcription factor hubs at single-molecule resolution."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "We found that endogenous EWS::FLI1 forms dynamic, sub-diffraction-limit hubs with mechanisms of dissolution that prevent the hubs from achieving macroscopic liquid-liquid phase separation."
    explanation: >-
      Endogenous hub imaging is reported in a bioRxiv preprint and is retained as a provisional refinement,
      not independently established consensus.
  - reference: PMID:23178492
    reference_title: "Mechanism and relevance of EWS/FLI-mediated transcriptional repression in Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Importantly, we demonstrated that the repressive function of EWS/FLI is absolutely required for the oncogenic function of the fusion."
    explanation: Supports including direct transcriptional repression in the canonical mechanism.
  - reference: PMID:40215343
    reference_title: "(GGAA)(3)-Based TF-PROTACs Enable Targeted Degradation of ETV6 to Inhibit Ewing Sarcoma Growth."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Recent studies identified ETV6 as a vulnerability in Ewing sarcoma, where it competes with EWS::FLI1 at short GGAA repeats to restrain EWS::FLI1 function."
    explanation: Supports ETV6 as a counter-regulatory modifier of the GGAA enhanceropathy.
- hypothesis_group_id: cell_of_origin_context_model
  hypothesis_label: Permissive developmental cell-of-origin model
  status: EMERGING
  description: >-
    Developmental timing and cell state influence fusion tolerance and transformation in human progenitor
    and animal models. Neural crest and early mesenchymal systems are experimentally permissive,
    but no unique human lineage or age of initiation is proven. IGF-1/YAP1 cooperation is established
    in a particular mouse-cell model, and inherited GGAA architecture modifies susceptibility at
    specific loci without establishing a universal permissive genotype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41136396
    reference_title: "EWS::FLI1 expression in human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells leads to transcriptional reprograming, defective DNA damage repair and Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "In summary, we show that EWS::FLI1 enforces an aberrant transcriptome and solely is able to endow transforming capacity when expressed in undifferentiated, early heMSCs."
    explanation: Supports the developmental-context hypothesis in embryonic mesenchymal stem cells.
  - reference: PMID:40080499
    reference_title: "YAP1 is a key regulator of EWS::FLI1-dependent malignant transformation upon IGF-1-mediated reprogramming of bone mesenchymal stem cells."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "We report that transient exposure to IGF-1 concentrations mimicking serum levels during puberty reprograms limb-derived mesenchymal cells of EWS::FLI1-mutant mice to stable transformation and tumorigenicity."
    explanation: Supports IGF-1/YAP1 signaling as a developmental cooperating mechanism.
  - reference: PMID:36787739
    reference_title: "Targeted long-read sequencing of the Ewing sarcoma 6p25.1 susceptibility locus identifies germline-somatic interactions with EWSR1-FLI1 binding."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "We propose that germline microsatellite variation at the 6p25.1 EwS susceptibility locus could impact downstream gene expression and EwS biology."
    explanation: Supports inherited GGAA microsatellite architecture as part of the permissive-context model.
- hypothesis_group_id: replication_stress_vulnerability_model
  hypothesis_label: Transcription-coupled replication stress vulnerability model
  status: EMERGING
  description: >-
    A superimposed vulnerability framework links fusion-driven R-loops, TOP1-stress-dependent DHX9
    sequestration, context-dependent BRCA1 impairment, SLFN11 fork arrest, PARP1-supported transcription
    and USP1-survivin stress buffering. A POLQ/MMEJ defect is supported by a preprint, and SLFN11-loss-associated
    lipid remodeling is a candidate resistance route. These mechanisms complement the canonical fusion
    model; experimental sensitivities do not establish uniform clinical HR deficiency or PARP-inhibitor
    benefit.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:29513652
    reference_title: "EWS-FLI1 increases transcription to cause R-loops and block BRCA1 repair in Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Here we show that Ewing sarcoma cells display alterations in regulation of damage-induced transcription, accumulation of R-loops and increased replication stress."
    explanation: Supports R-loop accumulation and replication stress downstream of EWS-FLI1 activity.
  - reference: PMID:40721661
    reference_title: "EWS::FLI1-DHX9 interaction promotes Ewing sarcoma sensitivity to DNA topoisomerase 1 poisons by altering R-loop metabolism."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "We discovered that EWS::FLI1 prevents the resolution of R-loops induced by these drugs via sequestering DHX9 helicase, ultimately resulting in R-loop accumulation, replication stress, and genome instability."
    explanation: Supports the DHX9-dependent R-loop arm of the vulnerability model.
  - reference: PMID:25779942
    reference_title: "SLFN11 Is a Transcriptional Target of EWS-FLI1 and a Determinant of Drug Response in Ewing Sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "RESULTS: EWS-FLI1 binds near the transcription start site of SLFN11 promoter and acts as a positive regulator of SLFN11 expression in Ewing sarcoma cells."
    explanation: Supports direct EWS-FLI1 activation of SLFN11 within this vulnerability model.
- hypothesis_group_id: cohesin_modified_high_risk_model
  hypothesis_label: STAG2/cohesin-modified high-risk enhancer model
  status: EMERGING
  description: >-
    STAG2 loss modifies fusion-dependent and independent chromatin contacts, PRC2 regulation and
    metastatic behavior. Repeat-class redistribution and selective multimeric enhancer amplification
    are supported by one recent perturbation study; earlier chromatin-contact studies are related
    but not exact independent replications. Prognostic associations depend on cohort and assay. COG
    diagnostic protein-loss/EFS data and Japanese sequencing/post-profiling-OS data measure different
    exposures and endpoints; the Japanese cohort had only three STAG2-mutant tumors. Their difference
    does not demonstrate an ancestry-specific mechanism or refute the COG association.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41950086
    reference_title: "STAG2 loss amplifies EWS-FLI1-driven microsatellite enhancer activity promoting Ewing sarcoma aggressiveness."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Together, these findings reveal that STAG2 loss reprograms, rather than globally attenuates, EWS-FLI1 function, amplifying a high-risk oncogenic transcriptional state in Ewing sarcoma."
    explanation: Supports the STAG2-modified high-risk enhancer model.
  - reference: PMID:39487368
    reference_title: "STAG2 loss in Ewing sarcoma alters enhancer-promoter contacts dependent and independent of EWS::FLI1."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Subsequent genomic profiling and high-resolution chromatin interaction data from Capture Hi-C indicated that cohesin-STAG2 facilitates communication between EWS::FLI1-bound long GGAA repeats, presumably acting as neoenhancers, and their target promoters."
    explanation: Supports STAG2-dependent enhancer-promoter communication at long GGAA repeats.
  - reference: PMID:36221002
    reference_title: "Adverse prognostic impact of the loss of STAG2 protein expression in patients with newly diagnosed localised Ewing sarcoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among patients with localised disease, 5-year event-free survival was 54% (95% CI 34-70%) and 75% (95% CI 63-84%) for patients with STAG2 loss vs. expression (P = 0.0034)."
    explanation: Supports the high-risk clinical association for STAG2 protein loss.
  - reference: PMID:41206913
    reference_title: "Analysis of comprehensive genomic profiling test for Ewing sarcoma in pediatric patients and adults using the nationwide clinical and genomic database in Japan."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "There was no significant difference in overall survival after genomic profiling test enrollment for STAG2 and TP53 mutations (P = .663 and P = .767), but those with CDKN2A and CDKN2B deletions had poor prognosis (P = .024 and P = .012)."
    explanation: >-
      The 81-patient Japanese profiling cohort found no significant STAG2 mutation association with
      post-enrollment OS. With only three STAG2-mutant cases and a different assay, endpoint and
      enrollment setting, this is not an ancestry-effect test or a direct replication of the COG
      diagnostic IHC analysis.
histopathology:
- name: Small Round Cell Tumor
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: Ewing Sarcoma
    term:
      id: NCIT:C4817
      label: Ewing Sarcoma
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  description: Ewing sarcoma is a small round cell tumor of bone or soft tissue.
  notes: >-
    Local NCIT places Ewing Sarcoma under both morphologic finding and neoplasm by special category
    hierarchies, and its definition explicitly captures the small round cell morphology.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: Histologically, most cases are made up of solid sheets of uniform small round cells with round nuclei containing finely stippled chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli, and scant clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm, with ill-defined cell borders
    explanation: >-
      The guideline describes characteristic morphology without asserting a proven neuroectodermal
      human origin.
- name: Homer Wright Rosette-like Formation
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: Homer Wright Rosette Formation
    term:
      id: NCIT:C35942
      label: Homer Wright Rosette Formation
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    Atypical Ewing sarcoma of bone can show rosette-like textures resembling Homer-Wright rosettes,
    reflecting neuroectodermal differentiation features in a minority of cases rather than a required
    diagnostic feature.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:3113717
    reference_title: "Small round blue cell sarcoma of bone mimicking atypical Ewing's sarcoma with neuroectodermal features. An analysis of five cases with immunohistochemical and electron microscopic support."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Ewing's sarcoma (ES) of bone may occasionally display rosette-like textures mimicking Homer-Wright ones, as seen in neuroectodermic neoplasms (neuroblastoma, peripheral neuroepithelioma)."
    explanation: >-
      Supports Homer Wright rosette-like formation as an occasional histopathologic pattern in atypical
      Ewing sarcoma of bone.
- name: High Grade Tumor
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: high grade
    term:
      id: NCIT:C14158
      label: High Grade
  frequency: VERY_FREQUENT
  description: >-
    Ewing sarcoma is managed as a high-grade sarcoma. Its small round cell morphology does not imply
    indolent disease; stage and treatment response provide additional risk information.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: the NCCN, ESMO and British Sarcoma Group (BSG) guidelines follow-up recommendations for high-grade sarcomas, including ES, vary
    explanation: >-
      The guideline explicitly includes Ewing sarcoma among high-grade sarcomas.
- name: Post-Chemotherapy Tumor Necrosis
  finding_term:
    preferred_term: tumor cell necrosis
    term:
      id: NCIT:C35957
      label: Tumor Cell Necrosis
  description: >-
    Tumor cell necrosis can be assessed in Ewing sarcoma resection specimens, especially after neoadjuvant
    chemotherapy. The degree of tumor necrosis is a clinically meaningful histologic response marker:
    greater than or equal to 90% tumor necrosis defines a good chemotherapy response in many studies
    and is associated with improved local recurrence-free survival.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:17177205
    reference_title: "Chemotherapy response is an important predictor of local recurrence in Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Patients with a good response to chemotherapy (> or = 90% tumor necrosis), had superior LRFS at 5 years (86% vs 51%, P = .015)."
    explanation: >-
      Supports post-chemotherapy tumor necrosis as an Ewing sarcoma histologic-response measure with
      prognostic significance.

phenotypes:
- category: Musculoskeletal
  name: Bone Pain
  frequency: FREQUENT
  diagnostic: true
  description: >-
    Localized bone pain is a common presenting symptom of osseous disease, sometimes intermittent
    or initially attributed to strain. Frequency varies with age, site and ascertainment; the cited
    75.3% estimate is from a single-center adult cohort, not a universal pediatric estimate.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Bone pain
    term:
      id: HP:0002653
      label: Bone pain
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34235109
    reference_title: "Outcomes of Adult Ewing Sarcoma Treated with Multimodality Therapy: A Single-Institute Experience."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Pain (75.3%) was the most common symptom at presentation."
    explanation: >-
      A 73-patient cohort restricted to adults reported pain in 75.3%; this supports the within-cohort
      frequency and common clinical presentation.
- category: Musculoskeletal
  name: Soft Tissue Mass / Localized Swelling
  diagnostic: true
  description: >-
    A palpable mass or localized swelling may develop as tumor extends through the bone cortex into
    surrounding soft tissues. The mass is often firm and may be tender or warm, and may initially
    be attributed to trauma or infection.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Soft tissue neoplasm
    term:
      id: HP:0031459
      label: Soft tissue neoplasm
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34235109
    reference_title: "Outcomes of Adult Ewing Sarcoma Treated with Multimodality Therapy: A Single-Institute Experience."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In this study, pain and swelling were the most common presenting complaints seen in 75.3% and 42.5% patients, respectively
    explanation: >-
      Adult single-center cohort supports swelling as a common presentation; no universal VERY_FREQUENT
      estimate is inferred.
- category: Constitutional
  name: Fever
  description: >-
    Fever is a possible constitutional symptom. Inflammatory presentations may overlap with osteomyelitis;
    fever is neither required nor specific for Ewing sarcoma.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Fever
    term:
      id: HP:0001945
      label: Fever
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34485689
    reference_title: "Educational Case: Ewing Sarcoma of Bone."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: When present, constitutional symptoms include unintentional weight loss, fatigue, anemia, and fevers.
    explanation: >-
      The didactic article general clinical discussion supports these nonspecific manifestations.
      This quote is not an observation in its fictional teaching case, and no symptom-specific frequency
      is inferred.
- category: Constitutional
  name: Weight Loss
  description: >-
    Unintentional weight loss can accompany Ewing sarcoma as a nonspecific constitutional symptom.
    No individual weight-loss frequency is established by the cited general clinical discussion.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Weight loss
    term:
      id: HP:0001824
      label: Weight loss
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34485689
    reference_title: "Educational Case: Ewing Sarcoma of Bone."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: When present, constitutional symptoms include unintentional weight loss, fatigue, anemia, and fevers.
    explanation: >-
      The didactic article general clinical discussion supports these nonspecific manifestations.
      This quote is not an observation in its fictional teaching case, and no symptom-specific frequency
      is inferred.
- category: Systemic
  name: Metastatic Disease
  frequency: OCCASIONAL
  description: >-
    About one quarter of patients have detectable metastases at diagnosis, predominantly in lung,
    bone and bone marrow. Prognosis depends on metastatic distribution, age and treatment. In the
    metastatic AEWS1221 trial, three-year event-free survival was 37.4% with VDC/IE and 39.1% with
    added ganitumab; these estimates are not five-year overall survival.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Neoplasm
    term:
      id: HP:0002664
      label: Neoplasm
  notes: >-
    HPO searches for metastasis and metastatic did not identify a disease-agnostic
    metastatic-neoplasm term; retrieved narrower terms describe other specific tumors
    or imaging findings. HP:0002664 is a broad neoplasm anchor, not an exact encoding
    of metastatic spread. The Ewing-specific meaning is retained in the phenotype name,
    description and metastatic-stage entry.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34235109
    reference_title: "Outcomes of Adult Ewing Sarcoma Treated with Multimodality Therapy: A Single-Institute Experience."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among 21 (28.8%) patients, the lung (61.9%) was the most common site of metastasis followed by the bone, bone marrow, and brain."
    explanation: >-
      Supports the OCCASIONAL frequency band (5-29%) for metastatic disease at presentation — 28.8%
      of this 73-patient cohort presented with metastases — and the stated pattern of spread to lung,
      bone, and bone marrow. This is the frequency evidence; the survival items below support the
      separate prognostic claim, not the frequency.
  - reference: PMID:36669140
    reference_title: "Randomized Phase III Trial of Ganitumab With Interval-Compressed Chemotherapy for Patients With Newly Diagnosed Metastatic Ewing Sarcoma: A Report From the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "The 3-year EFS estimates were 37.4% (95% CI, 29.3 to 45.5) for the standard arm and 39.1% (95% CI, 31.3 to 46.7) for the experimental arm (stratified EFS-event hazard ratio for experimental arm 1.00; 95% CI, 0.76 to 1.33; 1-sided, P = .50)."
    explanation: Provides precise 3-year EFS data from the COG AEWS1221 phase III trial for metastatic Ewing sarcoma.
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: Although only 25% of patients have obvious metastases at diagnosis
    explanation: >-
      The contemporary guideline supports the approximate presentation frequency.
- category: Musculoskeletal
  name: Pathologic Fracture
  description: >-
    Fractures can complicate osseous Ewing sarcoma at presentation or during and after treatment.
    A historical long-bone cohort reported fractures in 14/93 patients across the disease course,
    including many after radiation; this is not a disease-wide presentation frequency.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Pathologic fracture
    term:
      id: HP:0002756
      label: Pathologic fracture
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11902298
    reference_title: Fractures in pediatric Ewing sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Fracture occurred in 14 (15%) of 93 patients with long-bone ESFT, most commonly in the femur.
    explanation: >-
      Retrospective long-bone cohort supports the complication, with restricted anatomy and historical
      treatment.
  - reference: PMID:11902298
    reference_title: Fractures in pediatric Ewing sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Nine (64%) of the 14 fractures occurred after the start of radiotherapy, and three of these were associated with either local recurrence or second malignancy.
    explanation: >-
      Distinguishes disease-course fractures from presentation and treatment-associated fractures.
- category: Hematologic
  name: Anemia
  description: >-
    Anemia can accompany Ewing sarcoma but is nonspecific and must be distinguished from treatment
    toxicity and other causes. Marrow involvement is one possible context rather than a demonstrated
    cause in every patient.
  phenotype_term:
    preferred_term: Anemia
    term:
      id: HP:0001903
      label: Anemia
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25691401
    reference_title: "Diagnosis and treatment of Ewing sarcoma of the bone: a review article."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: Anemia and leukocytosis are often observed in ES
    explanation: >-
      Clinical review supports the manifestation without a precise frequency.
biochemical:
- name: EWS-FLI1 Fusion Detection
  notes: >-
    Molecular demonstration of a compatible FET-ETS fusion confirms the integrated diagnosis. RT-PCR
    or RNA-based sequencing can identify the fusion partner. EWSR1 break-apart FISH alone is insufficiently
    specific and can miss some rearrangements; a negative or isolated positive result must be interpreted
    with morphology and immunophenotype.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: Genetic confirmation is required for ES diagnosis.
    explanation: >-
      Defines the molecular-confirmation requirement.
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: All cases of ES harbor a FET-ETS fusion.
    explanation: >-
      Includes rare FUS-containing fusions and distinguishes other round-cell sarcomas.
- name: CD99 and NKX2.2 Immunoreactivity
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: Immunohistochemically, neoplastic cells show a membranous pattern of intense and diffuse CD99 expression
    explanation: >-
      The guideline identifies typical CD99 staining.
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: However, it is important to note that CD99 and NKX2.2 are not entirely specific for ES
    explanation: >-
      Explicit specificity limitation.
  notes: >-
    Diffuse membranous CD99 and nuclear NKX2.2 support Ewing sarcoma in the appropriate morphologic
    context. Both are imperfectly specific; neither replaces fusion characterization.
genetic:
- name: EWS-FLI1 Fusion
  association: Somatic Fusion Oncogene
  notes: >-
    EWSR1::FLI1 accounts for approximately 85% of cases; EWSR1::ERG and rare other FET-ETS fusions
    account for the remainder. Rare FUS-containing fusions mean that EWS-ETS is not an exhaustive
    molecular definition. These are acquired somatic drivers, not a Mendelian inheritance pattern.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:17250957
    reference_title: "The Biology of Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "It is associated in 85% of cases with the t(11;22)(q24:q12) chromosomal translocation that generates fusion of the 5' segment of the EWS gene with the 3' segment of the ETS family gene FLI-1."
    explanation: Directly confirms the 85% frequency of the t(11;22) translocation creating EWS-FLI1.
- name: STAG2
  association: Somatic Tumor Suppressor Mutation
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  frequency: 17%
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: STAG2
    term:
      id: hgnc:11355
      label: STAG2
  notes: >-
    STAG2 loss-of-function mutations and protein loss are overlapping but distinct secondary alterations.
    Mutation frequency was 17% in one whole-genome cohort; localized COG tumors showed protein loss
    in 29/108 by IHC. STAG2/TP53 co-mutation was associated with poor outcome. Mutual exclusivity
    with CDKN2A deletion was a cohort observation, not a biological impossibility of co-alteration.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25223734
    reference_title: "Genomic landscape of Ewing sarcoma defines an aggressive subtype with co-association of STAG2 and TP53 mutations."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Apart from whole chromosome arm copy-number changes, the most common somatic mutations were detected in STAG2 (17%), CDKN2A (12%), TP53 (7%), EZH2, BCOR, and ZMYM3 (2.7% each)."
    explanation: Establishes STAG2 as one of the most common recurrent somatic alterations in Ewing sarcoma.
  - reference: PMID:36221002
    reference_title: "Adverse prognostic impact of the loss of STAG2 protein expression in patients with newly diagnosed localised Ewing sarcoma: A report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Among patients with localised disease, 5-year event-free survival was 54% (95% CI 34-70%) and 75% (95% CI 63-84%) for patients with STAG2 loss vs. expression (P = 0.0034)."
    explanation: Supports the adverse clinical association of STAG2 protein loss in localized Ewing sarcoma.
- name: TP53
  association: Somatic Tumor Suppressor Mutation
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  frequency: 7%
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: TP53
    term:
      id: hgnc:11998
      label: TP53
  notes: >-
    TP53 is recurrently mutated in a minority of Ewing sarcomas and co-occurs with STAG2 mutation
    in an aggressive secondary-genetic subset.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25223734
    reference_title: "Genomic landscape of Ewing sarcoma defines an aggressive subtype with co-association of STAG2 and TP53 mutations."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In an expanded cohort of 299 patients with clinical data, we discovered that STAG2 and TP53 mutations are often concurrent and are associated with poor outcome."
    explanation: Supports TP53 mutation as part of the high-risk STAG2/TP53 co-altered Ewing sarcoma subset.
- name: CDKN2A
  association: Somatic Tumor Suppressor Deletion
  variant_origin: SOMATIC
  frequency: 12%
  gene_term:
    preferred_term: CDKN2A
    term:
      id: hgnc:1787
      label: CDKN2A
  notes: >-
    CDKN2A deletion is a recurrent secondary alteration. Its reported mutual exclusivity with STAG2
    mutation concerns copy-number loss in particular cohorts; absence of CDKN2A point mutations in
    an unarchived portal analysis does not independently verify that relationship.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:25223734
    reference_title: "Genomic landscape of Ewing sarcoma defines an aggressive subtype with co-association of STAG2 and TP53 mutations."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "Strikingly, STAG2 mutations and CDKN2A deletions were mutually exclusive, as confirmed in Ewing sarcoma cell lines."
    explanation: Supports CDKN2A deletion as a recurrent secondary alteration distinct from STAG2-mutant Ewing sarcoma.
treatments:
- name: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    Interval-compressed vincristine, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide alternating with ifosfamide
    and etoposide (VDC/IE), with growth-factor support and hematologic recovery criteria, is a standard
    systemic backbone. Randomized data support two-week over three-week scheduling in localized disease.
    Treatment is delivered before and after surgery and/or radiation.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C213450
      label: Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: vincristine
      term:
        id: CHEBI:28445
        label: vincristine
    - preferred_term: doxorubicin
      term:
        id: CHEBI:28748
        label: doxorubicin
    - preferred_term: cyclophosphamide
      term:
        id: CHEBI:4027
        label: cyclophosphamide
    - preferred_term: ifosfamide
      term:
        id: CHEBI:5864
        label: ifosfamide
    - preferred_term: etoposide
      term:
        id: CHEBI:4911
        label: etoposide
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:23091096
    reference_title: "Randomized controlled trial of interval-compressed chemotherapy for the treatment of localized Ewing sarcoma: a report from the Children's Oncology Group."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: For localized Ewing sarcoma, chemotherapy administered every 2 weeks is more effective than chemotherapy administered every 3 weeks, with no increase in toxicity.
    explanation: >-
      The randomized COG study supports interval compression; the conclusion applies to its localized-disease
      population.
  - reference: PMID:36522207
    reference_title: "Comparison of two chemotherapy regimens in patients with newly diagnosed Ewing sarcoma (EE2012): an open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Dose-intensive chemotherapy with vincristine, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, and etoposide is more effective, less toxic, and shorter in duration
    explanation: >-
      EE2012 randomized evidence supports the VDC/IE approach over VIDE induction. The protocol also
      admitted Ewing-like sarcomas, a scope consideration when applying the result to modern molecular
      entities.
- name: Surgical Resection
  description: >-
    Wide surgical resection with negative margins is preferred when feasible without excessive morbidity.
    Reconstruction may be needed for limb salvage.
  therapeutic_modality: SURGERY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Definitive Surgical Resection
    term:
      id: NCIT:C154430
      label: Definitive Surgical Resection
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39158802
    reference_title: Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of Ewing sarcoma (Spanish Sarcoma Research Group-GEIS).
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: surgery is the treatment of choice if tumor resection is possible with negative margins, without significant morbidity, and with a reasonable functional outcome.
    explanation: >-
      Contemporary guideline supports margin-negative resection when feasible; this avoids causal
      superiority claims from a confounded observational treatment comparison.
- name: Radiation Therapy
  description: >-
    Definitive radiation is used for unresectable tumors or when surgery would cause significant
    morbidity. Also used post-operatively for close or positive margins.
  therapeutic_modality: RADIOTHERAPY
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Radiation Therapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15313
      label: Radiation Therapy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33818887
    reference_title: "Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Standard treatment involves multiagent induction chemotherapy followed by local treatment with surgery, definitive radiation, or a combination of surgery and radiation followed by additional chemotherapy and consolidation local treatment to metastatic sites."
    explanation: Confirms the role of definitive radiation as a local treatment option in Ewing sarcoma management.
- name: Adjuvant Chemotherapy
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    Systemic chemotherapy continues after local control to treat occult disseminated disease. Duration
    and consolidation depend on protocol and risk group; a fixed 9-12-month duration is not applicable
    to all modern interval-compressed regimens.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15632
      label: Chemotherapy
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:33818887
    reference_title: "Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: "Standard treatment involves multiagent induction chemotherapy followed by local treatment with surgery, definitive radiation, or a combination of surgery and radiation followed by additional chemotherapy and consolidation local treatment to metastatic sites."
    explanation: The review describes continuation of systemic chemotherapy after local treatment.
- name: PARP Inhibitor Combination Therapy
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    PARP-inhibitor combinations remain investigational in recurrent/refractory Ewing sarcoma. Talazoparib
    plus temozolomide produced no objective responses in ten phase-2 Ewing patients. A later pediatric
    olaparib-irinotecan phase-I/II study reported two Ewing responses, with a 6.3% response rate
    in its evaluable Ewing cohort. These limited signals do not establish routine efficacy or a validated
    HR-deficiency biomarker.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: talazoparib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:231344
        label: talazoparib
      description: Partnered with temozolomide in ADVL1411; not a four-drug regimen.
    - preferred_term: temozolomide
      term:
        id: CHEBI:72564
        label: temozolomide
      description: Cytotoxic partner of talazoparib in ADVL1411.
    - preferred_term: olaparib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:83766
        label: olaparib
      description: Partnered with irinotecan in the separate AcSe-ESMART arm D regimen.
    - preferred_term: irinotecan
      term:
        id: CHEBI:80630
        label: irinotecan
      description: Cytotoxic partner of olaparib in AcSe-ESMART arm D.
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: PARP1-Supported Fusion Transcription
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      PARP inhibition interferes with PARP-dependent transcription and traps PARP-DNA complexes.
      Preclinical sensitivity is not equivalent to demonstrated patient benefit.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:26505995
      reference_title: "Combinations of PARP Inhibitors with Temozolomide Drive PARP1 Trapping and Apoptosis in Ewing's Sarcoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: Here, we show that PARP inhibitor sensitivity in Ewing's sarcoma cells is not through an apparent defect in DNA repair by HR, but through hypersensitivity to trapped PARP1-DNA complexes.
      explanation: >-
        Supports PARP trapping as a cellular mechanism.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:31724813
    reference_title: "Phase 1/2 trial of talazoparib in combination with temozolomide in children and adolescents with refractory/recurrent solid tumors including Ewing sarcoma: A Children's Oncology Group Phase 1 Consortium study (ADVL1411)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: "In phase 2, 0 of 10 EWS subjects experienced an objective response; two experienced prolonged SD."
    explanation: >-
      Clinical evidence supports feasibility but only partial therapeutic support because objective
      responses were not observed in the phase 2 Ewing cohort.
  - reference: PMID:41591981
    reference_title: "Phase I/II Study of the PARP Inhibitor Olaparib and Irinotecan in Children and Young Adults with Recurrent/Refractory Malignancies: Arm D of the AcSé-ESMART Trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: Two patients with Ewing sarcoma experienced a complete and a partial response for 10 and 42 cycles, respectively.
    explanation: >-
      Limited activity in a later phase-I/II combination trial; this does not establish general efficacy
      or attribute the effect uniquely to PARP inhibition.
- name: LSD1 Inhibitor Therapy
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    Seclidemstat (SP-2577) is an investigational LSD1-associated transcriptional modulator studied
    in fusion-positive sarcoma cells and trials. Laboratory activity links to fusion-dependent
    transcription, but clinical efficacy in Ewing sarcoma is unproven and preclinical xenograft
    activity has been limited.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: seclidemstat
      term:
        id: NCIT:C154328
        label: Seclidemstat
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: NuRD-LSD1 Transcriptional Repression
    treatment_effect: MODULATES
    description: >-
      Seclidemstat is intended to modulate LSD1-linked transcriptional and chromatin programs
      downstream of EWS-FLI1 and related FET fusion proteins.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40852926
      reference_title: "Seclidemstat (SP-2577) Induces Transcriptomic Reprogramming and Cytotoxicity in Multiple Fusion-Positive Sarcomas."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Seclidemstat recapitulated much of SP-2509 transcriptional activity in Ewing sarcoma."
      explanation: Supports seclidemstat modulation of the Ewing sarcoma transcriptional program linked to the LSD1 pathograph arm.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:40852926
    reference_title: "Seclidemstat (SP-2577) Induces Transcriptomic Reprogramming and Cytotoxicity in Multiple Fusion-Positive Sarcomas."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "Seclidemstat recapitulated much of SP-2509 transcriptional activity in Ewing sarcoma."
    explanation: >-
      This is an in-vitro pharmacology result. A paper mentioning a trial does not verify its
      current registry status or clinical efficacy.
  - reference: PMID:34453478
    reference_title: "In vivo evaluation of the lysine-specific demethylase (KDM1A/LSD1) inhibitor SP-2577 (Seclidemstat) against pediatric sarcoma preclinical models: A report from the Pediatric Preclinical Testing Consortium (PPTC)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: "SP-2577 (100 mg/kg/day × 28 days) statistically significantly (p < .05) inhibited growth of three of eight Ewing sarcoma (EwS), four of five rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), and four of six osteosarcoma (OS) xenografts."
    explanation: >-
      Supports in vivo preclinical activity in a subset of Ewing xenografts, but only partial
      support because the same abstract reports limited activity overall.
  notes: >-
    A July 2024 sponsor SEC filing states that the Ewing seclidemstat phase I/II trial was
    terminated to conserve cash. Later preclinical papers mentioning clinical trials do not
    establish continued recruitment or efficacy. Source:
    https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1615219/000161521924000071/flks-20240630.htm
- name: USP1 Inhibitor Therapy
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    USP1 inhibition is a preclinical targeted strategy aimed at the EWS-FLI1 induced USP1-survivin
    survival buffer that helps Ewing sarcoma cells tolerate endogenous replication stress and standard
    chemotherapy exposure.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: USP1 inhibitor
      description: >-
        Local NCIT/CHEBI search did not identify a USP1-specific inhibitor class; this uses the broader
        NCIT enzyme inhibitor class while preserving USP1 specificity in preferred_term.
      term:
        id: NCIT:C471
        label: Enzyme Inhibitor
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: USP1-Survivin Stress Buffering
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      USP1 inhibition blocks a survival adaptation within the replication-stress node by destabilizing
      the USP1-survivin axis and sensitizing cells to DNA damaging chemotherapy.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:37478161
      reference_title: "USP1 Expression Driven by EWS::FLI1 Transcription Factor Stabilizes Survivin and Mitigates Replication Stress in Ewing Sarcoma."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: "Notably, USP1 inhibition sensitizes cells to doxorubicin and etoposide treatment."
      explanation: >-
        Supports targeting the USP1-dependent replication-stress survival buffer in Ewing sarcoma
        cells.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37478161
    reference_title: "USP1 Expression Driven by EWS::FLI1 Transcription Factor Stabilizes Survivin and Mitigates Replication Stress in Ewing Sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "USP1 knockdown or inhibition arrests EWS cell growth and induces cell death by apoptosis."
    explanation: Supports USP1 inhibition as a preclinical targeted treatment concept in Ewing sarcoma.
- name: Dual PARP-HDAC Inhibition
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    The bifunctional compound kt-3283 has preclinical activity in Ewing cells and spheroids. It inhibits
    PARP1/2 and HDAC enzymes; these observations do not establish direct CHD4 inhibition or clinical
    efficacy.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:37279093
    reference_title: A Bifunctional PARP-HDAC Inhibitor with Activity in Ewing Sarcoma.
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: Here, we report the concept and characterization of a novel bifunctional PARPi (kt-3283) with dual activity toward PARP1/2 and HDAC enzymes in Ewing sarcoma cells.
    explanation: >-
      Preclinical dual-target pharmacology, distinct from clinical talazoparib/temozolomide.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: kt-3283
      description: NCIT and CHEBI searches for kt-3283, kt3283 and KT 3283 found no compound-specific term. The broader PARP-inhibitor class describes one experimentally measured activity of this single bifunctional compound; HDAC inhibition remains explicit in the treatment description. This is not talazoparib, olaparib or a combination of two agents.
      term:
        id: NCIT:C62554
        label: Poly (ADP-Ribose) Polymerase Inhibitor
  target_mechanisms:
  - target: PARP1-Supported Fusion Transcription
    treatment_effect: INHIBITS
    description: >-
      The compound inhibits PARP1/2 as one of its two measured enzymatic targets.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:37279093
      reference_title: A Bifunctional PARP-HDAC Inhibitor with Activity in Ewing Sarcoma.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      snippet: Here, we report the concept and characterization of a novel bifunctional PARPi (kt-3283) with dual activity toward PARP1/2 and HDAC enzymes in Ewing sarcoma cells.
      explanation: >-
        Preclinical dual-target pharmacology, distinct from clinical talazoparib/temozolomide.
- name: Cabozantinib in Advanced Disease
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    Cabozantinib, a MET/VEGFR2 inhibitor, showed activity in the single-arm CABONE phase-II trial
    in advanced Ewing sarcoma: 10/39 efficacy-evaluable patients had partial responses by six months.
    This is a salvage research option with toxicity and limited comparative evidence, not an established
    replacement for frontline multimodal therapy.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: Pharmacotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15986
      label: Pharmacotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: cabozantinib
      term:
        id: CHEBI:72317
        label: cabozantinib
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:32078813
    reference_title: "Cabozantinib in patients with advanced Ewing sarcoma or osteosarcoma (CABONE): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: In patients with Ewing sarcoma, ten (26%; 95% CI 13-42) of 39 patients had an objective response (all partial responses) by 6 months
    explanation: >-
      Single-arm phase-II activity among efficacy-evaluable advanced Ewing patients, not proof of
      survival benefit or frontline efficacy.
- name: High-Dose Ifosfamide for Recurrent or Refractory Disease
  therapeutic_modality: SMALL_MOLECULE
  description: >-
    The rEECur randomized salvage study provides comparative evidence favoring high-dose
    ifosfamide over topotecan-cyclophosphamide after earlier gemcitabine-docetaxel and
    irinotecan-temozolomide arms closed. The 2022 phase III conference report compared 73 patients
    per arm: median event-free survival was 5.7 versus 3.7 months and overall survival 16.8 versus
    10.4 months for ifosfamide versus topotecan-cyclophosphamide. Renal toxicity and
    encephalopathy constrain selection and monitoring; this does not establish universal
    suitability or cure.
  treatment_term:
    preferred_term: chemotherapy
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15632
      label: Chemotherapy
    therapeutic_agent:
    - preferred_term: ifosfamide
      term:
        id: CHEBI:5864
        label: ifosfamide
  evidence:
  - reference: DOI:10.1200/JCO.2022.40.17_suppl.LBA2
    reference_title: "Phase III assessment of topotecan and cyclophosphamide and high-dose ifosfamide in rEECur: An international randomized controlled trial of chemotherapy for the treatment of recurrent and primary refractory Ewing sarcoma (RR-ES)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: For the phase III comparison between TC and IFOS (both, 73 patients), median EFS was 3.7 months (95% CI, 2.1-6.2) for TC and 5.7 months (95% CI, 3.8-7.0) for IFOS. Median OS was 10.4 months (95% CI, 7.5-15.5) for TC and 16.8 months (95% CI, 11.1-25.8) for IFOS.
    explanation: >-
      Primary randomized conference abstract reports event-free and overall survival in the
      contemporaneous phase III comparison; EFS must not be relabeled as PFS.
  - reference: DOI:10.1200/JCO.2022.40.17_suppl.LBA2
    reference_title: "Phase III assessment of topotecan and cyclophosphamide and high-dose ifosfamide in rEECur: An international randomized controlled trial of chemotherapy for the treatment of recurrent and primary refractory Ewing sarcoma (RR-ES)."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: 'The main grade 3/4 adverse events (% patients with an event) for TC (left-hand values) compared with IFOS were: febrile neutropenia (26% vs. 25%), infections (8% vs. 14%), vomiting (1% vs. 1%), nausea (0% vs. 3%), diarrhea (1% vs. 1%), encephalopathy (0% vs. 7%), and renal toxicity (0% vs. 8%).'
    explanation: >-
      The comparative adverse-event data are relevant to salvage regimen selection.
  notes: >-
    The trial-team November 2025 update reports that carboplatin-etoposide closed in August 2024
    and the continuing comparison is ifosfamide with or without lenvatinib; the older guideline
    statement that carboplatin-etoposide remained under comparison is superseded. Source:
    https://www.ucl.ac.uk/medical-sciences/divisions/cancer/centres-and-networks/euro-ewing-consortium/clinical-trials/reecur

- name: Human embryonic mesenchymal stem cell EWS-FLI1 transformation model
  description: >-
    Early human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells transduced with EWS-FLI1 acquire an Ewing-like
    transcriptome. Tumor formation was tested separately in immunodeficient xenograft hosts. This
    engineered permissiveness differs from later MSC states tested in the study; it does not
    uniquely identify the human lineage of origin.

      label: mesenchymal stem cell

  - EWS-FLI1 transformation

  - target: Permissive Progenitor Cell State
    description: >-
      Demonstrates that only undifferentiated, early heMSCs (not adult MSCs or pediatric MSCs) fully
      support EWS-FLI1 transformation, linking progenitor developmental state to oncogenic
      permissiveness.
  - target: Context-Dependent BRCA1 Repair Impairment
    description: >-
      Measures altered BRCA1 expression, localization and damage-response phosphorylation alongside
      defective DNA repair in comet assays after EWS-FLI1 expression.
    relationship: MEASURES
    limitations: >-
      The study does not directly measure R-loop accumulation or isolate homologous-recombination
      repair with an HR-specific functional assay; those mechanisms cannot be inferred solely from
      BRCA1 and total DNA-damage readouts.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:41136396
    reference_title: "EWS::FLI1 expression in human embryonic mesenchymal stem cells leads to transcriptional reprograming, defective DNA damage repair and Ewing sarcoma."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: "In summary, we show that EWS::FLI1 enforces an aberrant transcriptome and solely is able to endow transforming capacity when expressed in undifferentiated, early heMSCs."
    explanation: >-
      The conclusion compares early embryonic MSCs with other tested MSC states. It does not exclude
      every other progenitor type or eliminate the animal component of tumorigenicity validation.
- name: BARD1-variant PSaRC318 and BARD1-depleted Ewing cells
  experimental_model_type: CELL_LINE
  namo_type: namo:TwoDCellCulture
  organism:
    preferred_term: human
